article_title: Biome 2.6.2 Adds Markdown, YAML and SCSS Support and Promotes 59 Nursery Lint Rules to Stable Groups

content_preview.title: Biome 2.6.2 Adds Markdown, YAML and SCSS Support and Promotes 59 Nursery Lint Rules to Stable Groups
content_preview.summary: Biome 2.6.2, published October 21, adds Markdown, YAML and SCSS support, a biome migrate stylelint command, recursive config extends and the promotion of 59 nursery rules.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

The Biome toolchain for JavaScript, TypeScript and web files published version 2.6.2 on October 21, 2026, according to the [GitHub release page](https://github.com/biomejs/biome/releases/tag/%40biomejs/biome%402.6.2). The release is listed as a set of minor changes and widens the file types Biome handles: its notes describe added support for Markdown, YAML and SCSS, alongside the promotion of 59 nursery lint rules to stable groups.

The previous Biome release the Herald covered was ...

editor_notes.content_quality: Concise, well-structured 550-word Briefing (range 300-800). Neutral tone, attributes all statements to the release notes or PRs, includes a What We Don't Know section. No AI self-reference.
editor_notes.source_verification: Snapshots source-0 (release page), source-1 (PR #11394), source-2 (PR #12132) read from sources/2026-10/biome-262-.../ and sanity-checked (200 OK, expected text present, suspicious_patterns null for all three). Live re-fetch via GitHub API: release body for @biomejs/biome@2.6.2 (published 2026-10-21T11:05:24Z), PR bodies and merge metadata. Release body confirms verbatim: 'has 100% compatibility against CommonMark' (line-wrapped in source), 'we plan to support them soon', 'more than 90% detected by our infrastructure', 'a few rules inspired by markdownlint', 'can now format and lint `.scss` files, and recognizes `.module.scss` files as CSS Modules'; opt-in frontmatter and cjkFriendlyEmphasis; proseWrap option; markdown.formatter.formatEmbeds enabled by default; YAML '.yaml and .yml' formatting. '59 nursery rules' recounted by hand from the raw body: correctness 13 + suspicious 19 + security 1 + performance 1 + complexity 7 + style 18 = 59, matches the 'Promoted 59 nursery rules to stable groups' line (PR #12108); correctness all recommended with error severity, useIframeSandbox security/error, useArraySome complexity - all confirmed. Other items confirmed: biome migrate stylelint with --write, biome inspect config, extends up to ten levels, --git flag and automatic Git VCS integration on biome init, --profile-type-inference for lint/check, Grit rules/presets/configs via manifest packages, Android Termux packages cli-android-arm64/x64. PR #11394 (merged 2026-08-27 into next): 'Linter and Formatter are enabled by default' and 'formatting always brings changes to a codebase' verbatim. PR #12132 (merged 2026-10-07 into main): 'due to the current limitations, we can't support cases like mixins, extend, etc.' and 'we expanded the documentation' verbatim. All three sources are first-party github.com. The internal Herald link /article/2026-10/16-biome-2515-... exists and the description matches. No claim relies on biomejs.dev (not cited). Versioning issue found: see concerns.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: All numbers, quotes and attributions verified. One headline-level imprecision: per the repository CHANGELOG at tag 2.6.2 (packages/@biomejs/biome/CHANGELOG.md) and the npm registry, the Markdown, YAML and SCSS support and the 59 promotions are listed under 2.6.0 (npm 2026-10-21T09:51Z); 2.6.1 (10:28Z) and 2.6.2 (11:08Z) were patch releases the same day with one patch change each. Only 2.6.2 has a GitHub release page, and that page aggregates the whole 2.6.0 minor-change list, which is what the article cites. The article is faithful to its cited page, but 'Biome 2.6.2 adds' attributes to the patch release features first shipped in 2.6.0 hours earlier. Same-day, same-series, single clarification: not a fabricated event, so correction-level rather than reject. Verb 'Adds' is accurate for the 2.6 series; Markdown is supported but CommonMark-only and enabled by default (not opt-in/experimental), SCSS is partial (no mixins/extend), all of which the article states.
editor_notes.originality: Earlier Biome 2.5.15 article (2026-10/16) covers a different release; this is a new release. Not a duplicate.
concerns: Headline and summary credit 2.6.2 with features that the repository changelog places in 2.6.0 (published about 75 minutes earlier on 2026-10-21); a clarification is filed. The cited release page does present them as 2.6.2 notes.
The article's statement that GFM is 'not yet covered' follows the notes; no later GFM work was checked beyond the cited sources.
recommendations: Check the repo CHANGELOG / npm version history when a GitHub release page covers a .x patch version in a new minor series, and name the minor release (e.g. 2.6.0) where the features first shipped.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, well-sourced release Briefing; every quote, count and attribution verified against first-party sources. Published with a clarification that the features first shipped in 2.6.0. Featured candidacy: 1 - accurate release coverage of a widely used developer toolchain adding three file types, for a defined developer audience
